Just passing along some information. Data centers need water for two critical operations: cooling and fire protection.

Data centers run lots of server banks which generate massive amounts of heat and require a consistent supply of cool air to keep the place from overheating and frying the equipment with all that precious data they collect on everyone. The air temperatures can be so high that water inside a fire protection system will boil, therefore many of the fire protection systems do not contain water which means there is a delay between the time a fire opens a fire sprinkler and when water is actually discharged.

Most data centers do not have an independent water supply and are connected to the municipal water supply. Typically it is controlled by a main valve located in the right of way at the road which was installed by the local municipality.
